A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on satisfiability across Pearl's Causal Hierarchy, despite the changed title. Their main texts, equations, tables, diagrams, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports complexity theorems, proofs, and hypothetical probability calculations, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V3 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. Its medical example and additional SCM illustrations are mathematical constructions, not empirical studies.

M1.justification: V3 removes the separate small-model decision procedure in v1 Algorithm 2, which guesses a bounded number of deterministic SCMs and checks a symbolic ETR formula. Algorithm 1 for linear interventional satisfiability remains unchanged, but removal of the separate solver substantially narrows the algorithmic scope.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The hypothetical medical example is retained in v3 Appendix B.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods or empirical baselines. Comparisons with prior complexity classifications are theoretical positioning.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol, including splits, metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or error studies. V3's additional SCM illustrations explain mathematical expressiveness and graph semantics.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. The relocated medical tables and calculations retain intervention probabilities 0.45 versus 0.40 and counterfactual probability 0.625. Changes to formal results concern theory.

T1.justification: V3 deletes v1's small-model definition, NEXP-completeness theorem, and supporting proofs in Section 4 and Appendix B.3. It adds Lemma 12's causal-ordering construction where v1 relied on an unresolved lemma reference. V3 Lemma 16 also corrects the conditional-probability numerator from P(delta) to P(delta, delta'). The principal unrestricted complexity classifications are retained.

C1.justification: V1's abstract and introduction advertise small-model NEXP-completeness as a main contribution; v3 removes that contribution. V3 instead foregrounds the first strictly increasing complexity hierarchy, qualified by complexity-separation assumptions in the introduction, and explicitly highlights validity consequences. The principal linear and polynomial classifications remain the same.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly qualifies strict complexity growth by separation assumptions, relates the probabilistic classification to MAP, and discusses implications for algorithm selection. V1's explanation of how restricting probabilistic support leaves exponential causal mechanisms disappears with the small-model section. The central interpretation contrasting expressiveness and complexity remains.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies executable implementations, hardware or software configurations, experimental hyperparameters, or code/data access instructions. The procedural changes concern mathematical decision algorithms and proofs.

R1.justification: V3 acknowledges Ibeling et al. (2024) as independently obtaining a variant of the polynomial-language result, adds Schaefer et al. (2024) and Suppes and Zanotti (1981), and drops Renegar (1992) with the small-model material. The principal relationship to earlier satisfiability research is retained.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title, substantially rewrites the contribution narrative, and reorganizes the linear results into separate probabilistic, interventional, and counterfactual subsections with accessible proof outlines. The medical example moves to Appendix B, formal definitions move to Appendix C, and polynomial languages receive their own main section.

P2.justification: V3 adopts the ICLR layout with a redesigned title/author block and running headers. It restyles and simplifies the summary table, relocates the four medical probability tables to Appendix B, adds two causal-DAG diagrams, and removes Algorithm 2. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 improves accessibility through the level-by-level presentation and causal diagrams, supplies the previously missing causal-ordering argument, and corrects the conditional-probability transformation. These support a modest improvement in exposition and proof completeness. The gain is tempered by removal of the separate small-model theorem and solver; the main complexity classifications themselves are unchanged.
